stories.brief: PayPal is set to cut about 70 jobs in its Tel Aviv development center, which is around a quarter of its workforce in Israel, as part of a wider global cost-cutting move and push into AI.
Blackstone has invested in Huskeys, a Tel Aviv startup that builds tools to manage and secure internet traffic created by AI agents and other non-human systems.
The Bank of Israel cut its benchmark rate to 3.25%, the lowest level in four years, while warning that the recovery is only partial and exporters are still feeling pressure from a strong shekel.

sources.title: Bank of Israel slashes rates to four-year low to bolster postwar economic rebound

stories.brief: Ben Gurion Airport and workers have agreed on steps to ease a post-strike backlog, but the airport still faces a shortage of staff before the busy holiday season.
OpenAI, Anthropic and other companies are warning that the world has only a short window to prepare for more advanced AI-driven cyberattacks.
AP reports that many Americans are traveling closer to home this summer, choosing road trips and shorter stays as higher airfares and gas prices make vacations more expensive.
A Smithsonian feature looks at palaka, the blocky Hawaiian workwear pattern that spread beyond labor clothes and became a symbol of local pride.
AP revisits the Turtle, David Bushnell’s one-person submarine from the American Revolution, an early attempt at a bomb-carrying underwater craft that failed in action but left a lasting legacy.
AP says small businesses in tourist towns are seeing more people stick closer to home, with day trips and road trips replacing longer vacations for many families.
A Tel Aviv firm says Russian-speaking hackers used an AI coding tool in a way that helped disguise attacks on at least seven companies.
